land.text: the old oligarchic republic of Genoa, overthrown in early June 1797

predecessors.note: 'On June 14, 1797, the Ligurian Republic was proclaimed, under the watchful care of Republican France'; the Ligurian page's infobox adds the Republic of Noli as a predecessor.

land.text: 'Following the Congress of Vienna, it was awarded to Piedmont-Sardinia and annexed on 3 January 1815', its territories forming the Duchy of Genoa

successors.note: The restored republic ended on 28 July 1814; the formal annexation is 3 January 1815. 1805-1814 the land was French (first-french-empire), which is why the life has a gap.

capitals.name: Genoa
capitals.note: Infobox capital Genoa; same seat in the restoration of 1814.

rulers.name: Girolamo Luigi Durazzo (doge)
rulers.title: doge
rulers.note: Infobox lists him as ruler 1802-1805; 'a doge was nominated for a 5-year term' under the second Constitution of 1802. No complete list was on the pages opened.

correction.text: 'most of the Ligurian region' plus the small Imperial fiefs of the House of Savoy inside its territory; the page does not name the part left out

keyframe_review.note: 2,339 km2 (1797-1798): Genoa and its coast between 8.35E and 10.05E. The page says the republic 'covered most of the Ligurian region' with the small Imperial fiefs of Savoy inside it; the Liguria region is 6,070 km2 in the gazetteer, so the shape is 0.39 of it. The page gives no area (infobox lacks one) and does not say which part of Liguria lay outside.
2,292 km2 for 1799, the 1797 extent less a sliver. Same correction: most of the Ligurian region. The year saw the Directory 'deposed on 7 December 1799', an internal change.

correction.text: 'most of the Ligurian region', the republic of 1800-1802

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1800-1802: Cliopatria has no shape between 1799 and 1803 although the page has the republic in these years ('briefly occupied by Austrian forces in 1800, but Napoleon soon returned with an army and retook it'; second Constitution 1802). The Liguria region as above.

correction.text: 'most of the Ligurian region', to its annexation by France in June 1805

keyframe_review.note: 3,461 km2 for 1803-1804: the shape grows west to 7.47E (the western Riviera), which no opened page explains (the page gives no 1803 change). Replaced by the Liguria region. Annexed by France in June 1805.

correction.text: the Genoese republic restored between 28 April and 28 July 1814

keyframe_review.note: 3,300 km2 for 1814: the republic restored 'between 28 April and 28 July' 1814 on the Genoese core. The Liguria region as above.

region.text: Genoa and 'most of the Ligurian region', the sister republic of France

ledger.note: 14 June 1797: Napoleon founds the Ligurian Republic at Genoa. 'formed by Napoleon on 14 June 1797'; the same page has 'Napoleon announced the founding of the Ligurian Republic on 6 June 1797'; the Genoa page: 'On June 14, 1797, the Ligurian Republic was proclaimed, under the watchful care of Republican France'. First Constitution 22 December 1797.

region.text: the Genoese republic occupied by Austrian forces

ledger.note: 1800: the Austrians take Genoa. 'The Republic was briefly occupied by Austrian forces in 1800, but Napoleon soon returned with an army and retook it.' The page gives no month and no siege.
1800: Napoleon retakes the republic. 'Napoleon soon returned with an army and retook it'; the page names no battle (Marengo is not on it) and no date.

region.text: annexed as the departements of the Apennins, Gênes and Montenotte

ledger.note: June 1805: France annexes the Ligurian Republic. 'In June 1805, the area was directly annexed by France as the departements of the Apennins, Gênes and Montenotte'; the territorial-evolution page lists 'The Ligurian Republic (formerly the Republic of Genoa) (1805)' and the Genoa page 'in 1805 it was annexed by France'.

region.text: the republic restored on the fall of Napoleon

ledger.note: 28 April 1814: the Ligurian Republic is restored. 'After the fall of Napoleon in 1814, the republic was briefly restored between 28 April and 28 July'; the Genoa page: 'Genoa temporarily regained independence as the Repubblica genovese'.

region.text: the Genoese territories awarded to Sardinia, forming the Duchy of Genoa

ledger.note: 28 July 1814: the restored republic ends. 'briefly restored between 28 April and 28 July'; 'Following the Congress of Vienna, it was awarded to Piedmont-Sardinia and annexed on 3 January 1815'. The page does not say who ended it on 28 July; the Congress of Vienna award is the Genoa page's: it 'assigned all Genoese territories' to Sardinia.

wars.name: Austrian occupation of Genoa

zones.text: the Genoese republic occupied by Austrian forces in 1800

wars.outcome: 'The Republic was briefly occupied by Austrian forces in 1800, but Napoleon soon returned with an army and retook it.'
wars.note: The page names no siege and no battle; the war it belongs to (the War of the Second Coalition) was not opened. In June 1798 the Ligurian rulers also 'led the people into war against the' (the sentence is cut in the fetched text); not recorded.

certainty.note: The old Genoese frontiers and the dated departments of the 1805 annexation; the Imperial fiefs inside the territory and the western Riviera are not delineated by any opened page.
No state: the land is French (first-french-empire); the span is kept so that the certainty covers the dossier's years.
The restored republic of 28 April to 28 July 1814 had no fixed frontier on the pages opened.

notes: Cliopatria row 'Ligurian Republic' 1797..1814 (four shapes: 1797-98 2,339 km2, 1799 2,292, 1803-04 3,461, 1814 3,300). All are well below the Liguria region (6,070 km2) although the page says 'most of the Ligurian region'; each is therefore marked adjust to the region. The state has a gap 1805-1813 (annexed to France, first-french-empire) and a short restoration in 1814, treated as one state with a loss and a gain; the restored republic (28 April to 28 July 1814) could be argued to be a new state. Page budget: 3 pages, with Convention of Montebello and Principality of Oneglia not loadable (url_not_found), so the western extension of the 1803 shape (to 7.47E), the Imperial fiefs of Savoy and the 1798 war of the rulers 'against the' (sentence cut) are not settled; the Genoa page is also silent on Oneglia, Savona and the Riviera. The relation of France to the republic (sister republic, client) is recorded as vassal_start in french-directory (1797) and continues under the Consulate; the Ligurian page's predecessor 'Republic of Noli' has no Cliopatria row and no dossier. Needs a dossier: first-french-empire (counterpart for 1805 and 1814, written by another part). The dates 6 June (announcement) and 14 June 1797 (formation) are both the page's; 14 June is used.
